questions.q: What are the three stages of deploying a model from the Foundry catalog?
options: Find & select, agree & customize, deploy & verify
Train, test, retrain
Download, compile, run locally
Subscribe, cancel, resubscribe
questions.explain: The deployment flow is: find and select a model, agree to terms and customize the deployment, then deploy and verify it comes up healthy.

questions.q: When does the terms-and-conditions step appear during deployment?
options: On every single deployment, with no exceptions
The first time you deploy a given partner/community model in a project
Only for models sold directly by Microsoft
Never — terms are agreed to once per Azure subscription, automatically
questions.explain: Models from partners and community show a terms step the first time you deploy them in a given project; subsequent deployments of the same model skip it.

questions.q: What does a managed compute deployment ask you to configure that other deployment options typically don't?
options: Your email address
The programming language of your application
Instance count and virtual machine size
A credit card number
questions.explain: Managed compute deployments require you to choose an instance count and a specific virtual machine SKU, since you're provisioning dedicated hardware.

questions.q: After a deployment finishes, what two status fields should you check?
options: CPU temperature and fan speed
Stock price and weather
Browser version and operating system
Provisioning state and deployment state
questions.explain: Provisioning state (Succeeded) confirms the resource was created; deployment state (Healthy) confirms the model is actually serving requests.

questions.q: What should you do before wiring a new deployment into application code?
options: Use the portal's Test tab to send a sample request first
Nothing — application code should always be the first test
Delete the deployment and recreate it
Change the deployment name five times
questions.explain: The portal's Test tab lets you confirm the deployment responds correctly before wiring it into any application code.
